title: High performance impact of `hint_screen_texture` and mipmaps.
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.5beta3, 4.4stable, 3.6.1stable ### System information Godot v4.5.beta3 - Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS 24.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) UHD Graphics (CML GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10510U CPU @ 1.80GHz (8 threads) - 15.28 GiB memory ### Issue description I am trying to implement some simple screen space effects for my 2D game (chromatic aberration, blur, bloom, nothing that would be too fancy these days), and noticed it became unplayable on my otherwise moderately performant intel laptop. From what I've been able to triage with my meager rendering knowledge, it comes down to one core problem: Sampling a screen texture on my integrated laptop GPU is _very_ performance heavy. Just adding a ColorRect with a shader that does nothing takes ~4ms if ran on a full screen window: ```gdshader shader_type canvas_item; uniform sampler2D screen_texture : hint_screen_texture, repeat_disable, filter_nearest; void fragment() { COLOR = textureLod(screen_texture, SCREEN_UV, 0.0); } ``` At first, I thought most of this must be some overhead for using the feature at all, but doing it twice in two canvas layers roughly doubles the cost to ~7ms, so there seems to be a linear correlation between screen resamples and processing time. With the sampler hint set to `filter_nearest_mipmap`, the performance is even worse, it takes around 8ms to do a simple screen resample, eating up half the frametime for a 60fps target. The compatibility renderer has very similar performance characteristics, so switching away from Forward+ doesn't seem to be a viable solution. I'm not sure if this is expected, a bug, or if I'm doing something dumb. What I'm doing here seems to be the accepted method for applying full screen effects (according to both google and the [docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/custom_postprocessing.html)). But since there is a full-screen shader running rendering everything in the first place, I really wouldn't expect such a hard performance hit just for trying to modify the pixel values a bit before blitting them to the screen. I'd be very thankful for any advice on how to do this smartly, or what else to test that could improve performance. ### Steps to reproduce Add a full screen canvas item, with a shader using a sampler with `hint_screen_texture`. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [screen-texture-lod.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21413796/screen-texture-lod.zip)
